items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4825

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend chapter 270 of the laws of 2008 authorizing the town
of Deerpark to issue bonds, in relation to extending such
authorization


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
To allow the Town of Deerpark (Orange County) to issue serial bonds on
or before June 30, 2010 in the amount of $859,988 to liquidate an
accumulated operating deficit.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Allows for the issuance of serial bonds in the above stated amount by
the above stated date in conformance with the provisions of the local
finance law (Section 10.10).

 EFFECTS OF PRESENT LAW WHICH THIS BILL WOULD ALTER :
Current law authorizes the issuance of $868,000 in bonds by the end of
June, 2009. This legislation slightly reduces the amount of the
necessary bond since it has been determined that the deficit that
needs to be liquidated is now $859,988 instead of $868,000. In
addition, it gives the Town another year to issue the bonds.

 JUSTIFICATION :
A new Town Supervisor took office in January, 2008 only to find
substantial financial mismanagement by the prior administration. The
deficit was created when the former Town Supervisor anticipated
funding of $297,500 from FEMA as a result of a flood in April, 2005.
The Town spent approximately $333,000 for the project but did not
complete it within the established timeframe, resulting in the loss of
funding.

Further, the Town's adopted budget for the fiscal year ending December
31, 2008 improperly included approximately $600,000 of non-existent
fund balance and $212,999 of over estimated revenues.  The current
Town Supervisor identified the problem and worked with the Board to
reduce the Town's budget by $333,376. Despite these modifications, the
Town's General and Highway funds experienced operating losses of
$556,129.

By letter to the Town Supervisor of April 13, 2009, Deputy Comptroller
Steven J. Hancox verified that the Town may issue bonds in an amount
not to exceed $859,988 to funds its General and Highway fund deficit.

The deficit was discovered, verified by the State Comptroller, and as
a result these bonds are necessary.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.
